# Analysis scope and workflow overview {#analysis-scope-and-workflow-overview}

## Analysis stages

This guide follows one paired mouse-brain section from normalized measurements
to individual and joint embeddings, regional markers, feature associations and
an exported report. It uses native Bioconductor containers and follows the original
[mouse-brain tutorial](https://genomicsmachinelearning.github.io/SpaMTP/articles/Multi-Omic_Mouse_Brain.html).
The table also points to replicate inference and pathway analysis, which need
the study design and identity references described in their respective sections.

| Stage | Main interface | Output |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Normalization | `normalizeSMData()` | A declared expression scale for each modality |
| Representation | `runMetabolicPCA()`, `runSpatialGraphPCA()`, `multiOmicIntegration()` | Individual, spatial and joint embeddings |
| Regional markers | `findAllDEMs(method = "markers")` | AUC, effect sizes, detection and spatial sensitivity |
| Replicate contrasts | `findAllDEMs(method = "replicate")` | Biological-replicate effects and uncertainty |
| Feature associations | `findCorrelatedFeatures()` | Raw and covariate-adjusted correlations |
| Pathways | `buildPathwayIndex()`, `createPathwayAssay()`, `findRegionalPathways()` | Identity-level expression, coverage and enrichment |
| Reporting | `renderSpaMTPReport()` | Linked figures, tables and analysis provenance |

## Demonstration datasets

We retain all 876 paired locations, 2,075 mass spectrometry imaging (MSI)
features and 32,285 RNA features in the archived striatal dataset, acquired
with a 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid (DHB) matrix and paired with Visium RNA.
The source is a coronal section from a 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA)-lesioned mouse (mouse 3, V11L12-038_B1;
[GSM7392311](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSM7392311)).
The original analysis selected these striatal locations from the source section.

This is a single section; the replicate-design section provides a call template
for studies with independent samples. The pinned
mouse resource downloads once (about 48 MB) and is cached. The
[gene and joint-pathway guide](Gene_Identifier_Mapping.html#joint-ms-and-rna-pathways)
contains the complementary human MSI/Xenium example and its acquisition and
identity-mapping details.

# Input modalities and study design {#input-modalities-and-study-design}

## Paired measurements and modality definitions

`x` is the mouse-brain `SpatialExperiment`. Its main assay stores MSI intensities;
`altExp(x, "SPT")` stores RNA at the same locations. `spec` declares each modality's
measurement type, input matrix (`layer`) and species.
For paired inputs, use unique feature and observation names, finite assay values,
and identical observation names and column order across modalities.

```{r inputs, message=FALSE}
library(SpaMTP)
library(SpatialExperiment)
library(SpaMTPData)
x <- spaMTPData("mouse_brain_dhb_striatum", version = "1.1.0")
spec <- list(
    main = list(type = "metabolomics", layer = "counts", species = "Mus musculus"),
    SPT = list(type = "transcriptomics", layer = "counts", species = "Mus musculus")
)
region_side_counts <- table(x$RegionLoupe, x$lesion)
region_side_counts
metadata(x)$SpaMTPData[c("resource", "version", "md5")]
```

## Anatomical labels and spatial layout

`RegionLoupe` contains archived anatomical labels: CP, caudoputamen; ACB,
nucleus accumbens; OT, olfactory tubercle; cc, corpus callosum; CTX, cortex;
LSX, lateral septal complex; and aco, anterior commissure, olfactory limb.
`lesion` labels the two sides. CP contains `r region_side_counts["CP", "intact"]`
intact-side and `r region_side_counts["CP", "lesioned"]` lesioned-side locations.
Groups with fewer than three locations are excluded from marker scoring.

`plotSpatialLabels()` reads these labels from `colData(x)` and positions each
location using `spatialCoords(x)`. Figure 7.\@ref(fig:input-spatial-layout)
locates the archived regions and lesion sides; y increases downwards to follow
the image orientation.

```{r input-spatial-layout, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.8, out.width="720px", fig.cap="Archived DHB/Visium striatal dataset. Each point is one of 876 paired locations; colour denotes the archived anatomical region and shape denotes lesion side. Axes are original image pixels, with y increasing downwards."}
plotSpatialLabels(x, "RegionLoupe",
    shapeBy = "lesion", pointSize = 1.2,
    legendTitle = "Archived region"
)
```

## Normalization and replication

`runSpaMTPWorkflow()` preserves input layers. Its default MSI/RNA transform is
`log2(1 + 10000 * value / column_sum)`; protein values use `log2(1 + value)`.
`normalizeSMData(..., "LogNormalize")` uses the same log2 transform.
Use `normalization = "none"` for already transformed inputs. Complete spectral
processing and RNA quality control beforehand.

Lesion sides, pixels and spatial blocks belong to one section. We preserve the
archived spatial coverage and compare both sides within the same archived CP
region. Results describe this specimen; population-level
inference requires independent biological samples.

# Individual, spatial and joint representations {#individual-spatial-and-joint-representations}

## Workflow settings

`fit` stores normalized modalities, embeddings, markers and associations.
Regional marker analysis retains all measured features.

| Argument | Meaning in this example |
|:--|:--|
| `group`, `regions` | Metadata columns for lesion side and archived anatomy |
| `clusters = 3` | Number of clusters in the primary representation |
| `npcs = 8`, `max_features = 1000` | Up to eight PCs from at most 1,000 variable features per modality |
| `association_features = 4` | Maximum marker/variable-feature anchors per modality pair, selected across regions |
| `coordinate_units` | Unit label for spatial coordinates and report provenance |
| `structure$primary = "spatial"` | Spatial representation used for downstream structure analysis |
| `structure$k_grid = c(3, 4)` | Candidate cluster counts used for sensitivity comparisons |
| `structure$reference = "RegionLoupe"` | Archived anatomy used to calculate adjusted Rand index (ARI) |
| `structure$umap = FALSE` | Display the first two components of each representation |
| `structure$stability_blocks = 3` | Three coordinate-based block omissions for clustering sensitivity |

```{r workflow}
fit <- runSpaMTPWorkflow(x, spec,
    group = "lesion", regions = "RegionLoupe",
    clusters = 3, npcs = 8, max_features = 1000, association_features = 4,
    coordinate_units = "original image pixels",
    structure = list(
        primary = "spatial", k_grid = c(3, 4),
        reference = "RegionLoupe", umap = FALSE,
        stability_blocks = 3
    )
)
metrics <- fit$structure$metrics
metrics[, c(
    "representation", "k", "approx_silhouette",
    "reference_ARI", "spatial_neighbor_agreement"
)]
```

Inspect `fit$qc` for modality-specific totals and detected-feature counts,
`fit$retained` for observation inclusion, and `fit$stages` for completion details.

## Representation construction

PCA and graph PCA use the same centred, scaled features, recorded by
`runMetabolicPCA(features = ...)`. `runSpatialGraphPCA()` builds a sparse
Laplacian per sample. `multiOmicIntegration()` concatenates standardized
embeddings with equal modality weights.

Graph PCA uses a sparse spatial graph and materialises the selected expression
matrix and solver output, including when the input assay is delayed.
Here `max_features = 1000` limits representation construction to 1,000 features
per modality; regional marker scoring uses all retained features.
See [scaling and memory use](Modern_Data_Access.html#scaling-and-memory-use)
for sizing larger analyses.

## Metric interpretation

Approximate silhouette measures separation within each representation; spatial-neighbor
agreement measures smoothness. [Adjusted Rand index (ARI)](https://mclust-org.github.io/mclust/reference/adjustedRandIndex.html)
compares clusters with `RegionLoupe`, with expected value zero for random partitions.
Here ARI ranges from `r sprintf("%.3f", min(metrics$reference_ARI))` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", max(metrics$reference_ARI))`, indicating low concordance with
archived anatomical labels in this section. CP accounts for
`r sum(x$RegionLoupe == "CP")` of `r ncol(x)` locations; smaller regions contribute
fewer observations. ARI remains chance-adjusted with unequal class sizes.

At the primary `k = 3`, joint PCA has silhouette
`r sprintf("%.3f", metrics$approx_silhouette[metrics$representation == "Joint / PCA" & metrics$k == 3])`,
compared with
`r sprintf("%.3f", metrics$approx_silhouette[metrics$representation == "main / PCA" & metrics$k == 3])`
for MSI and
`r sprintf("%.3f", metrics$approx_silhouette[metrics$representation == "SPT / PCA" & metrics$k == 3])`
for RNA. The joint representation has lower silhouette separation in this
dataset. Consider separation and spatial-neighbor agreement together when
selecting a representation. ARI evaluates correspondence with the declared
anatomical reference; the molecular maps below describe feature-level spatial
patterns within those regions.

Block omission refits clustering on fixed full-data embeddings to assess spatial
sensitivity. See the [report panels](#report-panels) for embeddings and partitions.

# Molecular patterns across the striatum

## Paired ion and transcript maps

`Penk` ([preproenkephalin](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/18619)) and `Tac1`
([tachykinin 1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/21333)) encode neuropeptide
precursors. We map their RNA alongside m/z 400.14659, the measured DHB ion
featured in the original tutorial (Figure 7.\@ref(fig:brain-molecular-maps)).

`brain` is the analysed experiment in `fit$object`. `plotSpatialFeature()` reads
the ion from the main experiment and the two transcripts from its paired RNA
experiment. Their `workflow` values use log2(1 + 10,000 × value / total), with
totals calculated from all features in each modality. Each panel retains its
own colour scale and the ion is labelled by measured m/z.

```{r brain-molecular-maps, fig.width=10.5, fig.height=4.7, message=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Paired ion and transcript maps across all 876 archived striatal locations. Point positions are shared across panels; axes show original image coordinates, with y increasing downwards. Each colour bar shows log2 library-size-normalized values on a feature-specific scale. The ion panel retains the measured m/z label; compound identification requires independent chemical evidence."}
brain <- fit$object
plotSpatialFeature(brain, c("mz-400.14659", "Penk", "Tac1"),
    assayName = "workflow", labels = c("m/z 400.14659", "Penk", "Tac1"),
    pointSize = 0.8, legendTitle = "log2 normalized value", ncol = 3
)
```

## Side differences within the caudoputamen

The table averages the normalized values displayed above within the CP
locations of each archived lesion side, for the ion in the main experiment and
the two genes in the paired RNA experiment.

```{r brain-cp-summary}
cp <- brain[, brain$RegionLoupe == "CP"]
table(cp$lesion)
cp_values <- cbind(
    `m/z 400.14659` = assay(cp, "workflow")["mz-400.14659", ],
    t(as.matrix(assay(altExp(cp, "SPT"), "workflow")[c("Penk", "Tac1"), ]))
)
aggregate(cp_values, by = list(lesion = cp$lesion), FUN = mean)
```

`Penk` and m/z 400.14659 are higher on the lesioned side of CP, whereas `Tac1`
is higher on the intact side. This comparison uses CP locations on both sides
and describes variation within this specimen.

# Regional marker characterization {#regional-marker-characterization}

## Marker scores and heatmap

`markers` contains MSI scores from `scoreMarkers()` in [scran](https://bioconductor.org/packages/scran): mean/minimum pairwise AUC,
standardized Cohen effects and non-zero detection fractions. Other eligible
regions receive equal weight. `logFC` is the difference on the selected scale.

`demsHeatmap(n = 2)` selects up to two positive markers per region by `mean_auc`
and plots row-standardized means in Figure 7.\@ref(fig:markers).
`logfc.threshold = 0` retains positive effects
on the selected expression scale.

```{r markers, fig.width=7, fig.height=5.5, out.width="700px", fig.cap="Regional MSI markers across all 876 archived mouse-brain locations. Rows are selected mass features and columns are eligible archived regions. Up to two positive markers per region are selected by mean AUC; duplicate selections appear once. Colours show row-standardized mean expression (z-scores), and the top strip identifies the region."}
markers <- workflowMarkers(fit, "main")
marker_order <- order(-markers$DEMs$mean_auc, -markers$DEMs$logFC,
    markers$DEMs$gene,
    na.last = TRUE
)
head(markers$DEMs[marker_order, c(
    "gene", "cluster", "logFC", "mean_auc",
    "min_auc", "mean_cohen", "direction_stability"
)])
demsHeatmap(markers,
    n = 2, only.pos = TRUE, logfc.threshold = 0,
    order.by = "mean_auc", fontsize_row = 9, fontsize_col = 10
)
```

## Spatial-block sensitivity

Leave-one-spatial-block-out fits keep region labels fixed and record effect
ranges, rank changes, effect-direction agreement (`direction_stability`) and
ineligible small-region fits.
These summaries describe sensitivity to the omission of individual spatial blocks.
A `direction_stability` of 1 means that every evaluable block-omission fit
preserved the full-data mean Cohen effect's sign.

# Inference across biological replicates {#inference-across-biological-replicates}

## Paired design across specimens

When independent specimens are available, `method = "replicate"` fits limma to
replicate means. `replicate` names the `colData()` column that identifies each
biological sample, and each contrast compares two levels of `ident`; set
`paired = TRUE` when every sample contributes both conditions. The template
below is shown unevaluated for this single-specimen example;
`help("findAllDEMs")` includes an executable example with a simulated paired
design.

```{r replicate-design, eval=FALSE}
replicate_de <- findAllDEMs(object,
    ident = "condition", assay = "main",
    assayName = "logcounts", method = "replicate", replicate = "patient_id",
    contrasts = list(treatment_control = list(
        numerator = "treated", denominator = "control", paired = TRUE
    ))
)
replicate_de$tests$treatment_control$table
```

## Replicate means and effect interpretation

This mode fits limma to equally weighted replicate means and requires at least
three complete pairs, or three replicates per arm for an unpaired design. `replicate_de` retains
the design, all tests, moderated intervals and BH-adjusted P values per modality
and contrast. `logFC` uses the supplied scale; RNA count inference may require a
separate pseudobulk model.

Single-section examples support descriptive spatial comparisons. Replicate
inference requires independent biological samples recorded in `patient_id` or
an equivalent sample identifier.

# Regional composition and feature associations {#regional-composition-and-feature-associations}

## Raw and adjusted correlations

`fit$associations` compares marker anchors with PCA-selected targets.
`findCorrelatedFeatures(covariates = ...)` records matched observations, raw
Pearson correlations and correlations after adjusting both features for the
declared sample, replicate and region fields.
In the returned table, `correlation` is covariate-adjusted, `correlation_raw`
uses the original values, and `observations` gives the number of matched locations.

```{r associations}
associations <- fit$associations[[1]]
head(associations[, c(
    "feature1", "feature2", "correlation_raw",
    "correlation", "observations"
)])
myelin_associations <- associations[associations$feature1 == "mz-264.268615" &
    associations$feature2 %in% c("Mbp", "Plp1", "Mobp"), ]
myelin_associations[, c("feature1", "feature2", "correlation_raw", "correlation")]
```

For m/z 264.268615 and the myelin-associated genes
[Mbp](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/17196),
[Plp1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/18823) and
[Mobp](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/17433), adjusted correlations range from
`r sprintf("%.2f", min(myelin_associations$correlation))` to
`r sprintf("%.2f", max(myelin_associations$correlation))`, and adjustment changes
each correlation by at most
`r sprintf("%.3f", max(abs(myelin_associations$correlation - myelin_associations$correlation_raw)))`.
The sample label is constant in this single section, so the adjustment here
removes differences between archived region labels. The positive associations
persist after that adjustment, supporting a spatial association with the myelin
expression program within this section. Spatial association alone does not
establish that the ion and the transcripts share a cellular source.

## Structure-constrained chemical follow-up

The spatial association motivates examining sphingoid-base chemistry.
[Sphingosine](https://www.kegg.jp/entry/C00319) has formula C18H37NO2.
[MassBank RP014702](https://massbank.eu/MassBank/RecordDisplay?id=MSBNK-BGC_Munich-RP014702)
records a fragment near m/z 264.2682 from a sphingosine standard.

This focused search includes **all C18H37NO2 records** in the pinned RaMP
table. `annotateSMILESStructure()` derives dehydration sites and the maximum
number of supported water losses for each structure. The index includes the
protonated ion and its one- and two-water-loss hypotheses. The measured m/z and
mean spectrum come from the same mouse section used in the full
[annotation example](Metabolite_Annotation_Pipeline.html#sphingosine-within-the-complete-candidate-search).

```{r myelin-structure-family, message=FALSE}
chemical_reference <- loadSpaMTPDatabase("chem_props", version = "3.0.7")$chem_props
structure_family <- chemical_reference[
    which(chemical_reference$mol_formula == "C18H37NO2"),
]
structure_family <- annotateSMILESStructure(structure_family)
family_structures <- unique(structure_family[c("iso_smiles", "max_water_losses")])
table(max_water_losses = family_structures$max_water_losses)

family_index <- buildMZAnnotationIndex(structure_family,
    polarity = "positive", maldi_matrix = "DHB",
    adducts = c("M+H", "M+H-H2O", "M+H-2H2O")
)
mean_spectrum <- data.frame(mz = rowData(x)$mz, intensity = rowMeans(counts(x)))
observed_mz <- rowData(x)["mz-264.268615", "mz"]
family_matches <- queryMZAnnotationIndex(observed_mz, family_index,
    ppm = 5, ms1_spectrum = mean_spectrum, min_score = 0
)
family_candidates <- family_matches[
    !duplicated(family_matches[, c("ramp_ids", "adduct")]),
]
```

The formula family contains `r nrow(structure_family)` database records and
`r nrow(family_structures)` distinct SMILES strings. `max_water_losses` counts
structurally supported dehydration steps; spectra are needed to establish which
fragments form under the acquisition conditions. The table below shows the
engine's mass-matched hypotheses for the actual
m/z `r sprintf("%.6f", observed_mz)` feature. `min_score = 0` exposes every
returned hypothesis before downstream score filtering. Repeated RaMP
identity/adduct pairs retain their highest-scoring database record in this display.

```{r myelin-engine-candidates}
family_candidates[, c(
    "metabolite_names", "adduct", "ppm_error", "score",
    "max_water_losses", "dehydration_status"
)]
```

These scores compare candidates within the selected molecular-formula family.
The annotation guide reports their positions among the
[complete database candidates](Metabolite_Annotation_Pipeline.html#sphingosine-within-the-complete-candidate-search),
including alternative formulae and adducts, and applies the pathway threshold.
The structural result and myelin association motivate targeted validation.
Related sphingolipids can yield the same fragment, so precursor-resolved MS/MS
and standards are needed to distinguish free sphingosine from other sources.

## Matched spatial views

The static report draws paired association figures for selected feature pairs.
Reports built with `interactive = TRUE` add standalone `plot3DFeature()` views
of the same features (see [report generation](#report-generation)). Read these
alongside the recorded covariates: spatial dependence and unmeasured structure
can also contribute to adjusted correlations.

# Identity mapping and pathway analysis {#identity-mapping-and-pathway-analysis}

The [gene and joint-pathway guide](Gene_Identifier_Mapping.html#joint-ms-and-rna-pathways)
executes the human MSI/Xenium pathway workflow: reconcile HGNC identities,
create compound and gene assays, rank every retained identity, test pathway
coverage, and display regional enrichment. Follow it when the question shifts
from individual spatial features to coordinated patterns across measured
pathway members.

For metabolites, `metabolite_ambiguity = "exclude"` omits features with multiple
candidate identities. Candidates, exclusions, aggregation weights and tested
membership remain inspectable in the identity assay and enrichment result.
HGNC applies to human genes; mouse genes need a species-specific or orthology
reference. The [annotation guide](Metabolite_Annotation_Pipeline.html#carry-the-annotation-threshold-into-real-pathway-analysis)
and installed mouse recipes demonstrate compound pathways.

# Extended reference workflows {#extended-reference-workflows}

## Reference scripts

The installed scripts extend the DHB/Visium and FMP-10/Visium analyses with
annotation, integration, pathways and reports. `prepare` and `run` are the
installed script paths; the output below shows their filenames.

```{r reference-recipes}
prepare <- system.file("workflows", "prepare_mouse_brain.R", package = "SpaMTP")
run <- system.file("workflows", "run_mouse_brain.R", package = "SpaMTP")
c(prepare = basename(prepare), run = basename(run))
```

Sourcing the two scripts defines `prepareMouseBrain()` and `runMouseBrain()`.
The full-data recipe below is shown unevaluated. It downloads the resources and
writes a complete analysis. `prepareMouseBrain()` resolves pinned SpaMTPData
1.1.0 resources into `input_dir`, and `runMouseBrain(case = "dhb")` runs the DHB
analysis from that directory into `report_dir`. Replace both placeholders with
new filesystem paths; existing output directories are protected from overwrite.

```{r reference-recipes-run, eval=FALSE}
source(prepare)
source(run)
input_dir <- "a_new_input_directory"
report_dir <- "a_new_report_directory"
prepareMouseBrain(outputDir = input_dir)
runMouseBrain(input_dir, outputDir = report_dir, case = "dhb")
```

An explicit `nativeDir` selects verified local files and defaults to offline mode.
`examples/pathway_network_mouse_brain_demo.R` provides the full-data network recipe.

## Spatial calibration and subset regeneration

FMP-10/Visium preparation requires a measured target radius in original image
coordinates via `spatialConfig`. For the registered V11L12-109_B1 pair only,
`extdata/mouse_brain_scalefactors.json` records Space Ranger's
`spot_diameter_fullres = 376.942` from [Vicari et al.](https://doi.org/10.17632/w7nw4km7xd.1).
Set `target_radius` to half that value for this pair. Other specimens require
their own calibration. Optional optical images need checked scale and orientation.

Both runners use pinned positive-mode DHB or FMP-10 annotation and exclude
ambiguous compound assignments. To regenerate the vignette subsets, source
`workflows/prepare_vignette_data.R` and call `prepareVignetteData()` with a new
output directory.

# Reports and exported results {#reports-and-exported-results}

## Report generation {#report-generation}

`renderSpaMTPReport()` writes the analysis, figures and tables into a new directory.
`report` is the resulting HTML path; `tempfile()` supplies a temporary directory
name here. Use a persistent new directory for an analysis you intend to retain.
This example writes a static report (`interactive = FALSE`) containing workflow
and paired association figures, tables and provenance. Setting
`interactive = TRUE` adds an offline region and
differential-expression explorer and standalone 3D feature views; the 3D views
require the rmarkdown package and Pandoc.

`plotSpaMTPWorkflow(fit)` lists the names of the available figures, and
`plotSpaMTPWorkflow(fit, which = ...)` draws one of them in the R session.

```{r report}
report <- renderSpaMTPReport(fit, tempfile("dhb-demo-report-"), interactive = FALSE)
basename(report)
plotSpaMTPWorkflow(fit)
```

## Embeddings and spatial partitions {#report-panels}

These panels use all 876 archived mouse-brain locations and are drawn from
`fit` with `plotSpaMTPWorkflow(fit, which = ...)`. Embedding colours in
Figure 7.\@ref(fig:report-embedding) show archived regions. Spatial colours in
Figure 7.\@ref(fig:report-spatial) show method-specific clusters. Each method
assigns its own cluster numbers.

```{r report-embedding, fig.width=12, fig.height=7.5, out.width="960px", fig.cap="Individual and joint embeddings of all 876 archived DHB/Visium locations. Each point is a paired location coloured by its archived anatomical region. Axes are the first two components of each representation; their scales are method-specific."}
plotSpaMTPWorkflow(fit, which = "structure_embedding")
```

```{r report-spatial, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, out.width="960px", fig.cap="Spatial partitions of the same 876 locations in original image coordinates. Colours indicate clusters fitted separately for each representation. Cluster numbers are local to each panel. Anatomical accuracy requires comparison with independent anatomical annotations."}
plotSpaMTPWorkflow(fit, which = "structure_spatial")
```

## Exported data and methods

The report includes region/feature tables, spatial views and CSV exports. The output directory retains the workflow RDS, stage inputs, settings,
reference provenance, checksums and PNG/PDF figures. Reports built with `interactive = TRUE` also provide the offline region and
differential-expression explorer and standalone 3D feature views in a browser that permits JavaScript.

Methods: [Bioconductor marker scoring](https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.basic/marker-detection.html)
and [GraphPCA](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-024-03429-x).
